correctness.rationale: With the full ternary alphabet fixed, a binary squarefree factor has length at most 3, so the remainder has length at most 3 and a complete arch has length 3 or 4. A long arch must be abac. Of the six long starts for a second arch, starting with c gives cc, starting with a gives an identical block or acac, and starting with b followed by c gives cbcb. The only surviving second arch is babc. Repeating the rule gives the unique triple and forces a square for a fourth. Grouping arches in fours gives n <= 4m - floor(m/4) + 3, with m the universality index by the arch criterion; the right side is ceil(15m/4) + 3, so 15m/4 > n-4. In particular m <= 4 forces n <= 18. A separate exact enumeration confirmed the triple is squarefree, the specified length-18 witness factors as 0102 | 012 | 1012 | 0102 | 101 and lacks 22222, and each of the 1,830 length-19 squarefree words contains all 243 length-five subsequences. The supplied verifier selects a length-18 example from its census; the independent check tested the particular witness printed in the finding.
residual_risks: The finite computation verifies the witnesses and threshold, not the all-length result; the boundary argument proves the latter. The 4/15 lower bound is not asserted to be asymptotically sharp.

evidence: Adamson's theorem 2.4 applies to unrestricted words but equates universality only with the number of arches; Grytczuk et al. give the length limit of three over two letters.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These general results give the arch criterion and the elementary four-position bound. Neither controls transitions across two complete arches, which is what improves the bound and deals with arbitrary finite, possibly nonextendible words.

value.rationale: The forced transition connects contiguous square avoidance with scattered-subsequence richness in the smallest alphabet supporting arbitrarily long squarefree words. It gives uniform quantitative control beyond the elementary four-position argument and resolves a natural first sharp forcing cutoff, without relying on a particular morphic construction.
residual_risks: No optimal asymptotic density, general alphabet analogue, or classification of all length-18 extremizers is established.
